title: SQL Server 2022 CU on APP01: stage it, Ian runs it, one restart, read the build back
symptom: KOR-APP01\SQLEXPRESS sits on an RTM-GDR build (16.0.1210.3) with no cumulative update; Windows Update does not offer the CU.
cause: SQL CUs are not offered through Windows Update for this instance; they come from the Microsoft Update Catalog.
check: SELECT SERVERPROPERTY('ProductVersion'), SERVERPROPERTY('ProductUpdateLevel'). 27 Oct before: 16.0.1210.3; after: 16.0.4305.5 CU27.
fix: Download the CU from the Update Catalog ON APP01 into D:\Installers, verify size + SHA-256 + Authenticode (27 Oct: KB5126934, 491,045,896 B, SHA-256 8F1A7F0A...E962E7E2). A copy-only CHECKSUM backup of KorStandards first, RESTORE VERIFYONLY. Ian runs the installer at the console (runbook on his Desktop). Setup exit 0 with 'Pending' = reboot required: restart APP01 once, then read version, 22/22 ONLINE, Agent, Worker, NetworkOps. After CU27 the PolyBase services, Launchpad and telemetry were Stopped (Automatic); nothing uses them. Proof: board rows 46 and 37.
plain: Remembers how APP01's SQL Server was safely brought up to CU27 and how to confirm it.

title: Two update installs on one server at once: one fails with 0x80240009 / 0x80240016
symptom: An install-updates run reports 'Installed 2 of 3, 1 failed' or '0 of 2, 2 failed' while someone is also installing updates on the box (27 Oct: Ian over RDP on FS01 and DC01 during NetworkOps' runs).
cause: Windows Update runs one install at a time; the second caller gets WU_E_OPERATIONINPROGRESS (0x80240009) or WU_E_INSTALL_NOT_ALLOWED (0x80240016). Nothing is broken.
check: Read the WU history on the box (Microsoft.Update.Session QueryHistory) and Get-HotFix for the KBs: 27 Oct FS01 showed the 20:53 failures then all 3 Succeeded at 20:55; DC01 had both KBs in Get-HotFix, build 26100.33650.
fix: Do not re-run blindly: read history + Get-HotFix + pending-restart flags first. If everything is in and nothing is pending, it is done. Agree who installs before starting; one installer per box.
plain: Explains why an update run can report failures when two people install at once, and how to check whether anything is really missing.

title: A NetworkOps 'Queued' reply is not a result: read the run before reporting it
symptom: networkops_run_fix answers 'Queued ... audited as action N' and the work is reported as started or done, but the action failed at once (27 Oct: install-updates-restart on FS01, confirmed=false, refused as disruptive and unconfirmed).
cause: Queuing and running are separate: refusals and failures land in the action's result, which the queued reply cannot show. A disruptive fix on a server is refused unless confirmed=true.
check: networkops_runs (or the device's actions) shows each action's real state: queued, running, done: <detail>, failed: <reason>.
fix: Report a netops action only from its result read back. Pass confirmed=true for an authorized disruptive fix. Owed code change: run_fix refuses an unconfirmed disruptive fix in its own reply. Proof: oversight.Mistake 69; action 11429 refused, 11430 ran.
plain: Reminds every session that a queued fix has not happened yet, and to check its result first.

title: The look guard: claims made from a command's silence or a summary line
symptom: A session says 'done', 'deployed' or 'went' when the only evidence is that a command returned, or a one-line summary, with no read of the changed thing.
cause: Momentum: the claim is written from the act, not from a look at its result.
check: tools/claude_look_guard.py (VD, 328c8ef and later) blocks Stop and SendMessage when a change kind has no later look of its kind (KorStandards oversight.LookRule). 16/16 tests at first release; a dry run on the 27 Oct transcript showed 0 unlooked.
fix: Do the look of the right kind, or word the message as only what was looked at. Its stated blind spot: it cannot judge whether the look was complete (one page of 26 satisfies it), and a NetworkOps action is not yet one of its change kinds (Mistake 69).
plain: Records why sessions are now stopped from claiming 'done' without checking, and what the check still cannot see.
